text:
Maya: anyone else seeing short p99 spikes in eu-west-2 after that small egress burst at ~14:03? not full noisy-neighbor but latency jumps for tenants in pool-dedicated-gpu-3
Oliver: saw it briefly in the dashboards, looks like a tiny burst of large batch jobs + outbound network throttling?
Maya: yeah batching + kv cache miss rate went up, so more tokens and more cross-AZ egress. p50 steady, p99 up ~180ms for ~3m.
Zara: sre-bot alerted on connection resets to proxy-az-b, count spiked ~600 over 2m, correlated w/ egress bump. link: https://grafana/redwood/d/abcd/proxy
SRE-bot: ALERT: proxy-az-b connection-reset-rate > 500 (2m window) — routing fallback engaged to regional-fallback.
Oliver: can we confirm routing policy picked fallback or we drained? router logs show fallback=true for ~2m.
Maya: i pulled a snippet from router logs:
```
2026-09-12T14:03:12Z router[main]: route id=tenant-42 -> pool=pool-dedicated-gpu-3 policy=latency-first fallback=regional-fallback reason=egress-burst
2026-09-12T14:04:05Z router[main]: route id=tenant-42 -> pool=dedicated-v2 policy=cost-first fallback=none
```
Oliver: hmm interesting that we fell back to dedicated-v2 which has different NIC shaping — might explain the short p99 tail. dedicated-v2s are on a different AZ NIC class.
Zara: possible thermal bump on a rack? but thermal alerts are clean. more likely NIC queue overflow + kernel offload hiccup.
Pete: quick mitigation: reduce soft-quota window for pool-dedicated-gpu-3 from 90s -> 30s to avoid prolonged routing stickiness. Also nudge router to prefer local-pool during small egress spikes.
Maya: agree on quota tweak. We should also add a microfallthrough policy so short-lived egress spikes don't flip tenant routing for >60s.
Oliver: proposed router patch (canary to eu-west-2 only):
```
policy: latency-first
soft_quota_window: 30s
micro_fallthrough: true
fallthrough_ttl: 45s
```
Zara: runbook step: if p99 > 150ms for 5m AND egress_spike > 300conn then revert fallthrough.
Maya: also, for longer-term: add NIC queue metrics into route scoring so we avoid pools with transient qdepth > 80%.
Pete: i'll open a short RFC and create canary: eu-west-2 only, start at 14:40, monitor for 30m.
SRE-bot: ACTION CREATED: RFC-3241 by pete — "micro-fallthrough and soft-quota tuning for burstlet behavior". Link: https://rfc.redwood/rfc-3241
Oliver: good. one more ask — let's tag workloads that use big batch inference as "egress-heavy" so routing can deprioritize them during egress pressure. quick label: `workload.egress=heavy`
Maya: tagging will help. Also add an alert rule that ties p99 to routing flips so we can correlate automatically.
Zara: i will add NIC qdepth dashboard and a quick alert.
Maya: thanks team. canary patch in 20. i'll follow up with post-canary note here. :thumbsup:
